claim: Rab GTPases were initially discovered in brain tissue.
source: Rab GTPases have been named for their initial discovery in brain tissue (Ras-like proteins from rat brain), where their abundance and diversity reflect neuronal adaptations and specialized membrane trafficking (Kiral et al., 2018; Touchot et al., 1987).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kiral et al., 2018 and Touchot et al., 1987.

claim: Rab GTPases function as key regulators of membrane trafficking between various membrane compartments.

claim: Some Rab GTPases have become gold standard identifiers of various organelles and vesicles in endocytic and secretory systems.

claim: A complete and comparative null mutant analysis of all Rab family members is currently not available for any multicellular organism.
